description: A four-in one-out scanner: four signals are crossfaded onto one output by a slider, so that neighbouring inputs overlap as it passes between them

params.text: Moves the scan across the four inputs; at each end only one input reaches the output, and between two positions both of the inputs it lies between reach it
Switched to + the SCAN CV knob adds the CV input to the slider, switched to - it subtracts it
Attenuates the SCAN CV input before it is added to the SCAN slider, 0% to 100%

inputs.text: Moves the scan, 5V peak to peak for the full sweep, added to the SCAN slider through the SCAN CV knob
One of the four signals being scanned; it reaches the output at whatever share the scan position gives it, and not at all when the scan is away from it

outputs.text: The four inputs added together at the shares the scan gives them, clipped at ±10V unless the menu turns that off

notes: the scan never quite reaches unity: each input peaks at about 0.89 of its voltage, which matches the hardware's crossfader.
menu: Clip Output ±10V — holds the output inside ±10V; on by default, and turning it off lets the sum run past the rails

inputs.0:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 1V.
